case_name: Jon K. Palsgaard and Kimberly A. Kelly v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Kimberly Kelly, physician disabled since March 2009, receiving SSD since 2010; same arguments rejected in Palsgaard, T.C. Memo. 2018-82.

adjustments: increased taxable Social Security disability benefits based on Form SSA-1099 showing $32,862
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Taxability of SSD benefits (claimed exclusion under §104(a)(1)-(3), no constructive receipt)

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner disabled by physical injury in March 2009
findings_of_fact.snippet: until March 2009, when she suffered a physical injury that left her disabled within the meaning of section 72(m)(7).
Petitioner received SSD benefits totaling $32,862 in 2019.

findings_of_fact.fact: Joint return reported SSD benefits of $3,214, of which $2,732 taxable
findings_of_fact.snippet: took the position that only $ 2,732 of that amount was subject to federal income tax.

findings_of_fact.fact: Benefits received under a government-sponsored insurance program, not by lawsuit or settlement
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner did not receive her SSD benefits by prosecution of a lawsuit or by settlement of litigation.

issues.question: Must petitioners include petitioner's 2019 Social Security disability benefits in gross income under §86, or are they excluded under §104(a)?
issues.holding: Includible: SSD benefits are social security benefits under §86(d)(1)(A); they are not 'damages' under §104(a)(2); other arguments rejected as in prior Palsgaard cases
issues.computable_reason: Legal classification: title II monthly benefits are §86 social security benefits, not §104 damages; taxable portion follows the §86 formula (not computed in opinion).

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent with respect to the deficiency and for petitioners with respect to the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty.
decision.summary: Deficiency sustained (SSD benefits taxable under §86); penalty conceded by respondent.

notes: Deficiency amount and taxable portion of benefits not stated in opinion; other income/MAGI needed for §86 computation not given. Unreported income foundation established via SSA-1099 transcript.
